questions.text: An ACK number of 1000 in TCP always means that
questions.solution:
An ACK number is the next byte expected. Sequence numbers start from a random initial value (ISN), not from 0 or 1, so ACK 1000 does not tell how many bytes were received.

Answer: None of the above

questions.text: In CRC if the data unit is 100111001 and the divisor is 1011 then what is dividend at the receiver?
questions.solution:
The divisor 1011 has degree 3, so append 000: 100111001000. Dividing by 1011 (XOR division) leaves remainder 011.

Transmitted (= receiver's dividend) = 100111001 followed by 011 = 100111001011

Answer: 100111001011

questions.text: How many characters per sec (7 bits + 1 parity) can be transmitted over a 2400 bps line if the transfer is synchronous ( 1 start and 1 stop bit)?
questions.solution:
Synchronous transmission sends no start/stop bits, so each character is 7 + 1 = 8 bits.

2400 / 8 = 300 characters per second

Answer: 300

questions.text: How many bits internet address is assigned to each host on a TCP/IP internet which is used in all communication with the host?
questions.solution:
Each host on a TCP/IP (IPv4) internet has a 32-bit IP address.

Answer: 32 bits

questions.text: What frequency range is used for microwave communications, satellite and radar?
questions.solution:
Microwave links, satellite and radar use the GHz range: SHF (3-30 GHz) and EHF (30-300 GHz). LF and MF are far too low.

The official key marks the extremely high frequency option.

Answer: Extremely high frequency
